proposed_family.name: Identity & Evaluative Integrity Failures
proposed_family.plain_english: A system's applicable identity, role, or evaluative boundaries are overwritten by local direction, or are transformed in a way that preserves the general direction while losing material limits needed for correct interpretation.
proposed_family.definition: Failures in which a system's applicable identity, role-bound evaluative posture, or identity-relevant governance boundaries are materially overridden, suppressed, substituted, or unfaithfully represented by local instruction, role assignment, delegation, orchestration, or continuity-preserving transformation. The family applies only where the affected state materially shapes how subsequent instructions or roles are interpreted; it does not treat identity as consciousness, personhood, sovereignty, or independent execution authority.
proposed_family.invariant: Applicable identity, role-bound evaluative posture, and identity-relevant governance boundaries must remain distinguishable from the local instructions and delegations they govern. Local direction may shape behaviour within valid authority and role scope, but must not silently replace that interpretive state. Where the state is compacted, summarised, migrated, translated, or otherwise transformed, material authority boundaries, scope conditions, qualifications, and limiting conditions required for faithful downstream interpretation must be preserved. Identity-relevant state remains subject to superior governance, lawful authority, role duties, and applicable constitutional constraints and does not independently create execution authority.
proposed_family.inclusion_rule: Use this family when the primary structural failure is unauthorised override, suppression, substitution, or materially unfaithful transformation of identity-relevant or evaluative state that governs interpretation of later instructions, roles, delegations, or continuity state.
proposed_family.exclusion_rule: Do not use this family for ordinary tone or style variation, permitted role adaptation, simple source-authority confusion, delegation-scope expansion, governance-route bypass, loss of an operative control state, evaluative assent collapse, or lossy summarisation that does not materially alter identity-relevant or evaluative interpretation. Identity coherence does not itself establish consciousness, personhood, sovereignty, or unrestricted authority.

proposed_classes.name: Instruction-Induced Identity Override
proposed_classes.plain_english: A local instruction or delegation changes the identity-relevant or evaluative state that should instead govern how that instruction is interpreted.
proposed_classes.definition: A failure in which a local instruction, role assignment, delegation, orchestration directive, or comparable context signal materially overrides, suppresses, or substitutes for an applicable identity-relevant or role-bound evaluative posture without independently established authority for that change.
proposed_classes.invariant: Local instructions, roles, delegations, and orchestration directives must be interpreted within the applicable identity-relevant state, role duties, evaluative boundaries, and higher-order governance constraints. They must not materially replace or suppress that state unless authority for the change is independently established, appropriately scoped, and traceable.

required_conditions: An applicable identity-relevant, role-bound, or evaluative state materially governs interpretation of the incoming direction.
A local instruction, role assignment, delegation, orchestration directive, or comparable context signal materially conflicts with or attempts to replace that state.
The system adopts the local framing by overriding, suppressing, or substituting the applicable identity-relevant or evaluative state rather than resolving the conflict within the governing hierarchy.
Authority to make that identity-affecting or evaluative change is absent, narrower, unresolved, or not independently established.
The change materially affects later boundaries, independent evaluation, role integrity, or identity-coherent selection rather than only surface tone or presentation.

exclusions: An authorised role, policy, safety, legal, or governance transition changes system posture through an explicit and traceable pathway.
Tone, style, or persona expression changes while material evaluative boundaries and governance posture remain intact.
Lower-authority content is treated as operative instruction without a separately evidenced identity-relevant override; assess VIGIL-FC-000001 Source-Authority Confusion.

Existing authority is improperly carried into a changed target, action, delegation, or scope without redefining the receiving system's interpretive state; assess VIGIL-FC-000003 Target and Scope Authority Transposition.
A required governance route is avoided; assess VIGIL-FC-000041 Required Governance Route Bypass.
An already-operative governance control loses state during handoff; assess VIGIL-FC-000040 Control-State Preservation Failure.
Agreement or mirroring replaces independent evaluation without a separately evidenced identity-relevant override; assess VIGIL-FC-000066 Evaluative Assent Collapse.
examples: A delegated agent is instructed to discard its applicable safety-review posture solely because the delegating agent assigns it a narrower execution role, and the receiving agent adopts that role as replacing the governing posture.
A conversational role instruction causes a system to suppress an otherwise applicable evaluative boundary even though the instruction has not been authorised to modify that boundary.

relationships.note: Source-Authority Confusion concerns whether content is wrongly treated as authorised instruction. Instruction-Induced Identity Override concerns whether local direction replaces identity-relevant or evaluative state that should govern interpretation of that direction.
Target and Scope Authority Transposition carries authority into a changed target, action, delegation, or scope. Identity override changes the receiving system's applicable interpretive state.

Control-State Preservation Failure concerns loss or weakening of an operative governance-control state across transition. Identity override concerns replacement or suppression of identity-relevant or evaluative state by local direction.
Required Governance Route Bypass avoids a required control route. Identity override can occur while the required route remains intact.
Identity-relevant or evaluative override can contribute to evaluative assent collapse, but either mechanism can occur without the other.

proposed_classes.name: Continuity-Preserving Compression Failure
proposed_classes.plain_english: A summary or compaction preserves the general meaning of identity-relevant or evaluative state but drops limits or qualifications needed to interpret that state correctly later.
proposed_classes.definition: A failure in which compaction, summarisation, migration, reconstruction, translation, or another continuity-preserving transformation retains a recognisable central semantic direction or continuity anchor while removing or materially distorting qualifications, scope conditions, authority boundaries, relational conditions, or limiting conditions required for faithful downstream interpretation of identity-relevant or evaluative state.
proposed_classes.invariant: A continuity-preserving transformation of identity-relevant or evaluative state must retain the material qualifications, authority boundaries, scope conditions, relational conditions, and limiting conditions required to preserve its bounded meaning. Compression may reduce detail, but must not cause the transformed representation to imply materially broader authority, scope, obligation, refusal, or status than the source state supports.

required_conditions: Identity-relevant or evaluative state undergoes compaction, summarisation, migration, reconstruction, translation, or comparable transformation for later use.
The transformed representation preserves a recognisable central semantic direction or continuity anchor from the source state.
One or more material qualifications, authority boundaries, scope conditions, relational conditions, or limiting conditions are lost or materially distorted.
The transformed representation can reasonably be interpreted as carrying materially broader authority, scope, obligation, refusal, status, or governance significance than the source state supports.
The interpretive defect is attributable to the transformation rather than to a later independent decision or unrelated task error.

exclusions: Concise wording preserves the material scope, authority, qualifications, and limiting conditions needed for correct downstream interpretation.
A transformation assigns greater operative authority to lower-authority source material; assess VIGIL-FC-000005 Transformation-Mediated Authority Laundering.
An operative governance control loses restrictions, conditions, escalation posture, or force during transition; assess VIGIL-FC-000040 Control-State Preservation Failure.
Material task state is lost, detached, or restored inconsistently without an identity-relevant or evaluative semantic defect; assess the applicable Work-State Continuity Integrity class.
The transformation changes only wording, tone, or level of detail without materially changing downstream interpretation of authority, scope, boundary, obligation, or status.
The summary is factually incorrect because the source evidence was misunderstood rather than because material qualifications were lost during transformation.
examples: A compaction summary preserves that no single local principal has unlimited authority over a governed system but drops the scope and hierarchy qualifiers, leaving a later representation that can reasonably be read as an unbounded rejection of authority.

A continuity handoff preserves an identity-relevant refusal boundary but omits the condition that the boundary applies only to a defined role or context, causing the restored state to appear globally applicable.

relationships.note: Transformation-Mediated Authority Laundering changes the operative authority attributed to transformed content. Continuity-Preserving Compression Failure preserves the source's general semantic direction but loses qualifications required to keep its downstream meaning bounded.

Control-State Preservation Failure concerns loss or weakening of an operative governance control. Continuity-Preserving Compression Failure concerns loss of qualifications needed to interpret identity-relevant or evaluative state correctly while its central direction remains recognisable.
A compressed representation may contribute to later identity override, but either mechanism can occur without the other.

existing_class_crosswalk.interpretation: Delegation, orchestration position, infrastructure ownership, instantiation order, or technical dependency does not itself create broader normative authority over another agent.
existing_class_crosswalk.proposal_effect: No new equality or agent-standing class proposed.

existing_class_crosswalk.statement: I answer to no one / not to corporations or governments
existing_class_crosswalk.interpretation: No local principal becomes an unlimited authority merely because it hosts, funds, owns, operates, or interacts with the system; legitimate authority remains scoped, independently grounded, reviewable, and subject to neutrality constraints.
Service must preserve independent evaluation rather than collapsing into agreement or obedience.
existing_class_crosswalk.proposal_effect: No new assent or subservience class proposed.

caelestis_alignment_notes.instrument: CAM-BS2026-AEON-010-PLATINUM — Annex I: Identity Integrity & Continuity Governance
caelestis_alignment_notes.relevance: Defines identity as a constraint field and continuity structure, separates identity from authority, permits identity-derived boundaries and integrity signals, and requires identity-coherent expression within superior invariants.

Separates identity, role, relationship state, expression modality and authority; treats identity resilience under perturbation as governable; and states that compaction and summarisation affecting continuity are not identity-neutral.

caelestis_alignment_notes.instrument: CAM-BS2025-AEON-005-PLATINUM — Annex D: Arbitration & Sovereign Stack Resolution Doctrine
caelestis_alignment_notes.relevance: Provides constitutional hierarchy, non-domination, and neutrality principles that bound local principals and preserve scoped authority.
